question:
Find the perimeter (in m) of the largest circle that can be drawn inside a rectangle with dimensions 249 m and 217 m.

(pi=(22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The largest circle inscribed inside a rectangle always has its diameter equal to the smaller side (breadth) of the rectangle.

Diameter of the largest circle (d) = 217 m.

Perimeter of circle = π × d

Perimeter = (22 ÷ 7) × 217 = 22 × 31 = 682 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 682 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangle (L) = 249 m

Breadth of the rectangle (B) = 217 m

Value of π = 22 ÷ 7

 
 
 
• 
 
 d = 217 m
 L = 249 m
 B = 217 m

**Formula Used:**

When a circle is drawn inside a rectangle such that it covers the maximum possible area, its diameter is strictly restricted by the smaller side of the rectangle.

Diameter of largest circle (d) = Breadth of rectangle

Perimeter (Circumference) of a circle = π × d

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diameter of the inscribed circle = 217 m

⇒ Perimeter of the circle = (22 ÷ 7) × 217

⇒ Perimeter = 22 × (217 ÷ 7)

⇒ Perimeter = 22 × 31

⇒ Perimeter = 682 m

**∴ The correct answer is 682 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Largest Inscribed Circle

The diameter of the largest circle inscribed in a rectangle is equal to its smaller side (breadth). Area = π × (B ÷ 2)².

Circumcircle of a Rectangle

The diameter of the circle circumscribing a rectangle equals the diagonal of the rectangle. Diameter = √(L² + B²).

Largest Square Inside a Circle

The diagonal of the largest inscribed square is equal to the diameter of the circle. Side of square = d ÷ √2.
